s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with motor and speech impairment
salient_findings: Episodes of spasms and tremors in the right hand and forearm
key_facts: Woman in her mid-60s
Initial carpal tunnel release surgery
Recurring tremors
Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells and cerebrospinal fluid contained lymphoma cells

shortlist.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Cadasil
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in white matter, consistent with small vessel disease

shortlist.label: Multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in white matter, which could indicate demyelination

shortlist.label: Hirayama disease
shortlist.why_kept: Initial symptoms of tremors and weakness in one arm, with progression over time

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells, along with the imaging findings of hyperintensities in the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: Typically associated with immunocompromised state and JC virus infection, not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Cadasil
rejected.why: Characterized by migraine with aura, stroke, and dementia, not matching the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: Typically shows contrast-enhancing lesions on MRI, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Hirayama disease
rejected.why: Characterized by focal amyotrophy, primarily affecting young males, not matching the patient's demographics or symptoms
